subject: Privatenet heartbeat mismatch — follow-up and runbook

From: John Miller <john.miller@harmonyhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+cloud@harmonyhealth.com
Date: 2027-07-31T08:12:00Z
Subject: Privatenet heartbeat mismatch — intermittent control channel drops since 07/31 04:50 PDT

Hi Vivek,

We started seeing control-channel drops on a subset of our private nodes this morning (first observed ~04:50 PDT). Symptoms: agents showing stale heartbeat, console shows nodes as "degraded" then reconnecting after ~30-90s. Impact: API calls from our internal services to the VPC endpoint got 5–10% elevated latency and occasional 500s.

Attached is a short sample of the agent heartbeat log (privatenet-heartbeat-sample.txt) and a timeline from our monitoring. Can you confirm whether any Redwood-side upgrade or config push occurred around that window? We are preparing to open an internal incident but wanted Redwood on the loop early.

Thanks,
John Miller
Platform Ops — Harmony Health
SOC-Triage: SOC-Triage@harmonyhealth.com

[attachment: privatenet-heartbeat-sample.txt (log snippet)]

Hi John — thanks for the heads up and the sample. Acknowledged and we’re triaging now.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- I’m pulling platform deploy logs to confirm any control-plane changes during the window you provided.
- Evelyn (runtime lead) will validate agent/server handshake compatibility.
- We’ll propose a short mitigation (forced agent fallback) if we confirm a version mismatch.

Can you also send: full agent logs for one affected node and the node-id you used in the sample? If you prefer, we can start a short call — we have availability at 09:00 PDT.

I’ll update here in 30–45 minutes with what we find.

— Vivek

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@harmonyhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, SOC-Triage@harmonyhealth.com
Date: 2027-07-31T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Privatenet heartbeat mismatch — initial triage and rollback plan

John / team — quick triage results from our runtime review: we observed a partial rollout of the private-agent v2.1.4 on 2027-07-31 04:33 PDT to a small subset of nodes in your tenancy (can confirm node-ids in logs). v2.1.4 introduced a heartbeat metadata field (hb_seq_v2) that older control-plane handlers treat as unexpected, causing a short parsing delay and a defensive reconnect in our agent handshake logic. On healthy networks this manifests as a ~30–90s transient reconnection like you saw.

Recommended immediate actions (short window fix):
- Force agent fallback to v2.1.3 for the affected node group. This is a low-risk server-side flag we can push from your private control plane.
- Enable temporary increased heartbeat timeout on your agent-side config (15s -> 60s) while we validate symmetrically.

If you’d prefer, we can execute the fallback for you — we would do a rolling revert across the subset, monitor for 60 minutes, and then coordinate a controlled reintroduce of the v2.1.4 changes once we patch the parser.

I’ll wait for your go. We’ve flagged an internal bug INF-8421 and started a limited test harness to reproduce.

— Evelyn
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Privatenet heartbeat mismatch — initial triage and rollback plan

Evelyn, Vivek — thank you. We executed the fallback to v2.1.3 on the affected node group at 01:45 PDT (automation triggered by your script). Reconnect behavior improved markedly; nodes moved to healthy state and latency returned to baseline for most traffic. We did still observe intermittent ~10s lag on two nodes — logs attached (privatenet-heartbeat-logs-20270731.zip).

Next asks:
- Can Redwood preserve these logs and include them in the postmortem?
- What’s the ETA for the parser patch and a safe re-roll to v2.1.4?

We are available for a quick postmortem call tomorrow 09:00 PDT.

Thanks,
John
Platform Ops — Harmony Health

Subject: Re: Privatenet heartbeat mismatch — summary, runbook link, and next steps

John— thanks for running the fallback and for the logs. Summary and immediate items below: 

What happened (short): partial rollout of agent v2.1.4 included an added heartbeat field that older control-plane handlers did not tolerate; result was transient reconnections for a subset of nodes in your private network.

What we did:
- Identified the root cause and flagged bug INF-8421.
- Coordinated a rolling revert to v2.1.3 for affected node group.
- Preserved logs you provided and captured server-side traces for the same timeframe.

Action items (owners):
- Redwood (Evelyn / Aditya): patch parser and validate compatibility tests (ETA: 2027-08-05 EOD).
- Redwood (Vivek): schedule controlled re-roll with Harmony (target window 2027-08-07 02:00–04:00 PDT).
- Harmony (John): share any additional node IDs if further affected nodes are discovered.
- Joint: postmortem meeting scheduled for 2027-08-03 09:00 PDT (calendar invite sent).

Runbook + artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/privatenet/harmony/runbook-v2 (we pushed a runbook diff — runbook-diff-v2.md — that lists the temporary timeout knob and a rollback checklist).

I’ll follow up after the patch lands with a recommended test plan and a short playbook for preventing similar releases into mixed-version fleets.

— Lauren
Sr. Product Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@harmonyhealth.com>, SOC-Triage@harmonyhealth.com
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T11:15:00Z
Subject: Postmortem follow-up: Privatenet heartbeat mismatch — closure and preventive fixes

Hi John / Harmony team — thank you again for partnering closely during this incident. Quick postmortem summary and closure items: 

Timeline (shortened):
- 2027-07-31 04:33 PDT: partial rollout of private-agent v2.1.4 to a canary slice in your tenancy.
- 2027-07-31 04:50 PDT: first control-channel drops observed by Harmony monitoring.
- 2027-07-31 09:00 PDT: Redwood triage confirms heartbeat metadata mismatch; proposed rolling fallback to v2.1.3.
- 2027-08-01 01:45 PDT: Harmony executed fallback; nodes largely recovered.

Root cause: a backward-incompatible heartbeat field (hb_seq_v2) was included in v2.1.4 without a tolerant parser in the older control-plane handler; mixed-version fleets experienced transient reconnects. Bug INF-8421 opened.

Work completed:
- Preserved customer-provided logs (privatenet-heartbeat-logs-20270731.zip) and server traces; linked to INF-8421.
- Implemented parser tolerance and added unit + integration tests to cover heartbeat schema variations. Patch PR: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-8421.
- Updated runbook with a temporary timeout knob and a safe rollback checklist (runbook-diff-v2.md).

Planned preventive measures:
- Deployment gating: require compatibility validation on mixed-version test harness before canary rollouts (owner: Runtime).
- Health-probe: add early-detection metric for heartbeat parsing errors with an alert to both Redwood SRE and customer Ops.
- Release notes: expand breaking-change callouts for agent-server contract changes.

Requested customer asks:
- If you can share the two node-ids that still showed the residual ~10s lag, we’ll pull deeper traces and schedule a targeted validation.
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to run the 02:00–04:00 PDT controlled re-roll or to own a dry-run with your team first.

Attachments: runbook-diff-v2.md (walks through the rollback and timeout knob).

If acceptable, consider this issue closed once we confirm the residual node validation (owner: Redwood). We’ll update INF-8421 with the final validation results and keep the runbook in the shared drive.

Appreciate the partnership — we’ll follow through on the patch timeline and the planned re-roll window.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0193
